evidence_items.locator: Commissioner Geoffrey Starks statement, paragraph beginning 'In January'
evidence_items.explanation: The surrounding paragraph identifies calls to New Hampshire primary voters urging them to skip voting. This supports the election-threat component, without proving an effect on the result.

evidence_items.publisher: Federal Bureau of Investigation, Internet Crime Complaint Center
evidence_items.explanation: The alert documents reports of manipulated imagery used in extortion, including increased victim reporting as of April 2023. It supports the existence of recurring abuse but does not establish how widespread deepfake scams were in April 2024.

evidence_items.locator: Paragraph describing selection and initial meetings; membership list above
evidence_items.explanation: The membership list gives major AI company leaders advisory roles alongside academics, civil-rights representatives and public officials. That establishes industry access, but neither proves policy capture nor establishes independent control.

evidence_items.publisher: Office of US Senator Amy Klobuchar
evidence_items.explanation: This supports the limited finding that the specified protective election bills were still awaiting committee consideration. It cannot establish that no qualifying protective federal law existed anywhere in the statute book.

evidence_items.locator: Section II, paragraph 3; application to AI explained in paragraphs 2 and 5
evidence_items.explanation: The ruling confirms that existing robocall protections cover AI-generated voices. This qualifies any suggestion of complete federal inaction, but applying an existing statute is not passage of new protective AI legislation.

unresolved_gaps: The retrieved legislative material does not provide a complete provision-level inventory sufficient to establish the absence of every qualifying protective federal law by April 27, 2024.
Advisory membership establishes access but does not demonstrate that industry interests controlled federal AI policy.
The official alerts establish real abuse but provide no adequate prevalence measure for the claim that deepfake scams were widespread at the post date.
